ANO-1000.explanation_text: Refrigeration in this zone ran at nearly three times its normal overnight draw for two straight hours in the middle of the night, then dropped back to normal. There was no business activity and the outdoor temperature was actually falling, so nothing about the site's operations or the weather explains the extra load. The most likely cause is cooling equipment struggling and running far longer than it should to hold temperature, which warrants sending a technician to inspect the unit before it fails outright or product is put at risk.

ANO-1001.explanation_text: Refrigeration draw jumped to roughly three times normal in the middle of the night and stayed there for three straight hours, with no business activity to explain it and outdoor temperatures actually falling during that window. That pattern points to the cooling equipment running almost continuously because it cannot hold temperature, most likely a struggling compressor. This warrants a technician visit, as continued hard running risks a full failure and product loss.

ANO-1002.explanation_text: The unit jumped to roughly double its normal draw almost instantly and held there for two full hours, then settled at a level still well above where it had been running beforehand. Outdoor conditions were mild and actually cooling off during that window, so there was no cooling demand to justify the extra energy. That pattern points to the air-handling side struggling or failing rather than normal morning operation, and it warrants a technician visit before the hotter part of the season loads the unit further.

ANO-1003.explanation_text: The refrigeration compressors jumped to roughly two and a half times their normal draw and held there steadily for about two hours before settling back, while outdoor conditions stayed flat — so the weather did not drive it. A sustained step up in power on a cooling system with no matching change in conditions usually means the compressors were working much harder than needed, such as struggling to hold temperature or cycling abnormally. It is worth sending a technician to inspect the compressor bank, since an early-stage mechanical or control problem often looks exactly like this before it fails outright.

ANO-1004.explanation_text: The refrigeration unit jumped abruptly to more than double its normal draw and held there steadily for two full hours before dropping back, rather than ramping up and down with the day's workload or the outside temperature. That flat, elevated plateau is the signature of a cooling compressor running hard and continuously to hold temperature, which usually means it is struggling or short-cycling. Worth sending a technician to inspect the unit, since a compressor working this hard can fail outright and put stored product at risk.

ANO-1005.explanation_text: The unit's power draw jumped to roughly double its normal overnight level and stayed there for two full hours before dropping back, even though the outdoor temperature was falling at the time. Cooling demand was decreasing, so there is no business or weather reason for the unit to work harder, and the size of the reading is well within what the equipment can physically draw, ruling out a metering glitch. A sudden step up in load that holds steady points to the air-handling side struggling or failing, so the unit should be inspected.

ANO-1006.explanation_text: Overnight, with no staff activity and outdoor temperatures actually falling, the refrigeration unit jumped to more than double its normal draw and held there steadily for two hours before dropping back. That kind of sustained, high, flat load with no business or weather trigger points to the cooling equipment struggling to hold temperature and running hard to compensate. This warrants a technician visit, as continued operation in this state risks a full failure and product loss.

ANO-1007.explanation_text: The lighting circuit jumped sharply early on a weekend morning and, although it eased back, it settled at a level noticeably higher than normal rather than returning to where it started. That pattern points to lights being switched on by the control system and not fully switching off again, which is a scheduling or control problem rather than normal business activity. Worth having someone check the lighting timers and sensors on this zone, but it is not urgent and does not need an emergency call-out.

ANO-1008.explanation_text: The unit's power draw jumped sharply to more than double its normal level and stayed there for two hours before dropping back, even though outdoor conditions were mild and had actually cooled slightly during that window. Because the extra load cannot be explained by heat or by any change in site activity, the most likely cause is the unit's air-moving equipment struggling or short-cycling and forcing the system to work far harder than needed. This warrants a technician visit to inspect the unit before the load returns or worsens during hotter weather.

ANO-1009.explanation_text: Power draw on this refrigeration zone jumped sharply and then stayed high for a full eight hours instead of easing back down, and the outdoor conditions were mild enough that weather cannot account for it. A cooling unit that runs continuously at elevated power like this is usually struggling to hold temperature, most often due to a failing compressor. Recommend dispatching a technician before the problem worsens or product is put at risk.

ANO-1010.explanation_text: The cooling system is running harder during an unusually warm overnight period, and its load falls away steadily as the outside air cools. That tracking with temperature is exactly what a healthy HVAC unit does, rather than the flat, stuck-on pattern a fault produces. No technician visit is warranted, though it is worth a quick check that the load returns to normal once the heat breaks.

ANO-1011.explanation_text: Consumption on this air handling unit stepped up sharply in the early hours and then climbed further instead of settling back, even as the outdoor air was getting cooler. That combination - rising power draw while the cooling demand is falling, on a quiet weekend night with no activity in the building - points to the unit itself working harder than it should rather than responding to conditions. This is the signature of a failing air-moving component, and it should be inspected before it runs unattended through the coming hot day.

ANO-1012.explanation_text: The refrigeration compressors jumped sharply in the early hours and stayed high for several hours instead of settling back down, even as outdoor temperatures fell. Overnight is the quietest period for the site, so there is no business or weather reason for the extra load — it points to compressors running much harder than needed to hold temperature. This warrants a technician visit before the warmer part of the day adds further strain.
